Foundation

Brand Essence

Clearing exists to bring clarity, accuracy, and defensible compliance to the most complex part of running a short-term rental business: the money. Every brand decision flows from this single idea.

"Clearing stands for clarity in every dollar."
Purpose-built for trust accounting, compliance, and the operators who take both seriously.
— Core brand promise

What we are

The financial operating layer for STR

An AI-powered trust accounting and bookkeeping automation platform built specifically for short-term rental property managers. We turn reservation-driven chaos into accurate books, compliant distributions, and audit-ready reporting.

What we're not

Not generic accounting software. Not a PMS.

We are not a general-purpose bookkeeping tool retrofitted for STR. We are not a property management system. We are the purpose-built financial layer that handles the complexity no PMS was designed to solve.

Why it matters

STR finance is structurally complex

OTAs bundle reservation revenue and net fees. Payout timing varies. Owners demand clean statements. Trust accounting rules require funds tracked by property and stakeholder. No PMS was built to solve this. Clearing was.

Mission

Help property managers close their books faster than ever before — with full visibility and accounting accuracy across every dollar, every property, and every stakeholder.

Purpose

To be the financial source of truth in the STR stack. The layer that gives operators, owners, accountants, and vendors confidence that every dollar is accurate, reconciled, and moving exactly where it should — and provably so.

Where Clearing fits competitively

Every stakeholder sees exactly what they need — from the same financial source of truth. Clearing's position is deliberate: more rigorous than PMS-native accounting, more accessible than pure accounting platforms.

PlatformPositioning leanWhat they miss
VRPlatformAccounting correctness and compliance depthAccessibility; often too technical for operators without finance teams
TopkeyExpense workflows; now leaning into trust accountingNarrow — misses the full financial lifecycle and stakeholder flows
ClearingHow money moves across the entire system, amongst all stakeholders — clean, clear, defensible, and accurateOur opportunity: own the intersection of rigor and clarity. Not too technical. Not too narrow.

What Clearing covers that the brand must reflect

Bookkeeping + Reconciliation

Clearing automates both. Bookkeeping organizes the financial picture. Reconciliation verifies it. Both matter — and they are not the same thing. Messaging must reflect this distinction.

Scaling operations

Clearing is built for operators who are growing. Multi-owner complexity, portfolio expansion, M&A, and mixed accounting models — Clearing handles what spreadsheets can't.

Financial lifecycle

From the first booking to month-end close. Trust accounting, reconciliation integrity, audit-ready reports, and stakeholder distributions — the full financial arc, not just the payout moment.

Portability

Keeping accounting outside the PMS means operators keep their financial history when they switch tech. Clearing makes PMS migration dramatically easier — a major standalone value proposition.

Complexity handling

Multi-owner structures, co-hosts, mixed management models, different payout logic per property — Clearing handles accounting complexity that generic tools weren't designed for.

Enterprise credibility

Audit-ready reporting, role-based access, financial controls, and reconciliation integrity give finance leads and accountants the professional-grade foundation they require.

Strategy

Market Positioning

How Clearing defines its category, its role in the STR ecosystem, and what makes it the only platform built to handle the full financial lifecycle the way STR operators and their accountants actually need.

Positioning Statement
For STR operators, accounting professionals, and their teams who manage the complexity of reservation-driven money movement, Clearing is the AI-powered trust accounting and bookkeeping automation platform that transforms complex money flows into accurate books, audit-ready reporting, and confident stakeholder distributions — purpose-built to complete the STR stack, not compete with it.
Category

AI Trust Accounting for STR

A category Clearing owns. We define it through education and proof — not just claims. Trust accounting is both a regulatory concept and a brand signal: we take the fiduciary responsibility seriously.

Differentiator

Built for STR complexity at scale

Three-way reconciliation across bookings, bank activity, and the general ledger. Every dollar, verified. Multi-stakeholder visibility. Audit-ready at every stage of the financial lifecycle.

Role in stack

The portable financial layer

Your PMS runs operations. Clearing keeps the books — independently, accurately, and portably. Operators who keep accounting in Clearing keep their financial history when they change anything else.

Communication

Messaging System

A hierarchy of messages that ensures everyone communicates with precision, regardless of channel. Use Tier 1 everywhere. Build down to Tier 3 for detailed product conversations.

Tier 1 — Core Claim (use everywhere)
AI-powered trust accounting for short-term rentals.
Use in headlines, introductions, bios, and anywhere Clearing needs a single-line explanation.
Tier 2 — Value Proposition (use in mid-funnel)
Your PMS runs operations. Clearing keeps your books in order.
Use when explaining where Clearing fits in the operator's existing stack.
Tier 3 — Proof Points (use in product conversations)
From bookkeeping and reconciliation to reporting and distributions — every dollar, accounted for.
Use when demonstrating depth: bookkeeping, reconciliation, expense management, owner statements, vendor payments, trust accounting, ACH payouts, audit-ready exports.

The PMS & Portability Narrative

ℹ
Updated framing (V2): Clearing's narrative has been refined. We no longer use language that attacks PMS platforms — but we do actively communicate the value of keeping accounting independent and portable. These are not contradictory positions. We can be partner-respectful while clearly articulating why a dedicated financial layer is more powerful, more flexible, and more durable than accounting inside the PMS.

✓ Say this

Your PMS is built for operations. Clearing is built for the money — and keeping those two layers separate gives you something valuable: portability.
If you ever change your PMS, your Clearing data stays yours. Your financial history, your audit trail, your owner records — all intact. That's a big deal.
Clearing works alongside leading PMS platforms. You don't lose what's in your PMS — you add a financial layer that actually knows how to handle the money.
No operator wants to find out their accounting is locked inside a PMS they want to leave. Clearing makes switching your tech stack a financial non-event.

✕ Don't say this

"PMS platforms can't do accounting." (True in many cases, but adversarial framing.)
"Your PMS is the problem." — Never position a PMS as failing.
Any language that directly attacks a named PMS in external content.
Anything that makes an operator feel bad about their current setup — we meet them where they are.

Visual Identity

Imagery & Layout

Clearing's visual language is product-first. The platform UI is the most powerful visual asset — it shows rather than tells. All imagery must reinforce accuracy, precision, and clarity.

✓ Use this

Actual Clearing product screenshots — payout reconciliation, owner statements, transaction feeds, and audit trails.
Money-flow diagrams showing how funds move across OTAs, Clearing, owners, vendors, and bank accounts.
Dark navy gradient backgrounds with teal accents for hero and brand contexts.
Abstract data visualization: bar charts, flow nodes, clean dashboards that suggest financial order.
Rounded surfaces (12-16px border radius), subtle shadows, polished fintech feel throughout.

✕ Avoid

Generic stock photography of accountants, spreadsheets, or office workers.
Lifestyle photography of vacation rental properties — that is the PMS's visual language, not ours.
Decorative illustrations that don't connect to the product or financial theme.
Busy, cluttered layouts — Clearing's design principle is precision and spaciousness.
More than 3 brand colors in a single composition.

Design principle: A real Airbnb payout breakdown — reconciled, categorized, and audit-ready in the Clearing UI — communicates more than any headline. Prioritize real product visuals in every context where they are available.

Tone of Voice

Voice Attributes

Clearing speaks to operators, accountants, and finance leads who are experienced and detail-oriented. They have been burned by complexity and inaccuracy before. Our voice earns trust by being precise, calm, and rigorous — without becoming heavy or corporate.

AttributeWhat it meansIn practice
PreciseUse exact, concrete language for workflows and outcomes."Booking and revenue reconciliation across OTAs" not "easy accounting."
CalmSteady confidence, not manufactured urgency.Let accuracy and clarity sell themselves. Urgency can be real; fear-based panic is not our voice.
TrustworthyEvery claim is grounded. No superlatives without proof."Three-way reconciliation across bookings, bank activity, and the general ledger" not "best-in-class accounting."
RigorousAccounting professionals need to feel the discipline.Use: audit-ready, role-based access, financial controls, reconciliation integrity. These are credibility signals, not jargon.
Operator-awareSpeak the language of STR finance.We say "trust accounting," "owner distributions," "payout reconciliation" — not generic accounting terms.
ClearExplain complexity simply without dumbing it down.If a sentence needs a second read, rewrite it. Financial rigour should feel accessible, not intimidating.
Tone of Voice

Writing Rules

Standards every piece of Clearing content must meet before it goes out. Apply to website copy, emails, social, product UI, and any external-facing internal communications.

✓ Always do this

Lead with outcomes. "Close your books in hours" before "automated reconciliation engine."
Use STR-specific workflow language: trust accounting, payout reconciliation, bookkeeping, owner distributions, ACH, audit trail, three-way reconciliation.
Include enterprise credibility signals naturally: audit-ready, role-based access, financial controls, reconciliation integrity, general ledger.
Be specific. "$40+ hours/month down to under 20" is more powerful than "saves significant time."
Write in active voice. "Clearing reconciles your payouts" not "payouts are reconciled."
Distinguish between bookkeeping and reconciliation — they are related but not the same. Use both where relevant.

✕ Never do this

Use manufacturing fear as the primary driver. Urgency that is grounded in real pain is fine; panic-based language is not Clearing's voice.
Directly attack PMS platforms by name or implication in external content.
Overstate the AI. Describe what it produces (clean, reconciled, audit-ready books) — not what it is.
Use generic accounting software language: "end-to-end platform," "comprehensive financial management solution."
Use em dashes anywhere in copy. Use commas, periods, or colons instead.
Write paragraphs that could apply to any fintech. Every sentence should only make sense coming from Clearing.

On urgency and fear

Fear is a real motivator in accounting and compliance contexts. Content pieces that speak honestly to the risk of inaccurate books, audit exposure, or losing financial history in a PMS migration can be more effective — and are entirely appropriate when grounded in genuine stakes. The line is between real operational pain (which we can speak to directly) and manufactured panic (which we avoid). A prospect who realizes their current process can't survive an audit is ready to act. We can meet that moment honestly.

Audience

Who We Serve

Clearing serves four distinct audiences, each with a different relationship to the money. Tailor messaging to the audience — but every segment should clearly see themselves in the brand and feel the accounting rigor that matters to them.

🏢
STR Operators & Property Managers
Primary buyer — most important audience
  • Managing 10-200+ properties; finance workflow has become a constraint on growth
  • Spending 20-40+ hours/month on manual reconciliation, statements, and payout matching
  • Using PMS platforms; wants a financial layer that integrates cleanly and works independently
  • Scaling their portfolio: needs tools that handle growing complexity, multi-owner structures, and mixed accounting models
  • Messaging: lead with speed of close, accuracy, peace of mind, and scalability as they grow
📊
Finance Leads, Accountants & Bookkeepers
Power user — technical champion — growing in importance
  • Responsible for compliance, trust accounting accuracy, and year-end close
  • Need role-based access, audit trails, clean exports, and reconciliation integrity
  • Evaluates platforms on financial controls, general ledger accuracy, and audit-readiness
  • May be an internal hire or external bookkeeper invited to the platform with their own access
  • Messaging: lead with trust accounting rigor, three-way reconciliation, P&L accuracy, and audit-ready reporting
🏡
Homeowners & Investors
End beneficiary — retention driver
  • Invited to their own read-only portal to review statements, reservations, and balances
  • Want transparency without complexity — they need to trust the numbers without doing the math
  • Their experience of Clearing reflects directly on the property manager's brand and credibility
  • Messaging: lead with visibility, clarity, and confidence that their investment is being handled correctly
🔧
Vendors & Service Providers
Payment recipient — ecosystem participant
  • Invited to submit invoices via their own vendor portal
  • Care about getting paid accurately and on time — platform features are irrelevant to them
  • Their experience validates the operator's financial professionalism to third parties
  • Messaging: lead with simplicity, payment speed, and transparent status
Ecosystem

PMS Partnership & Portability

PMS platforms are important go-to-market partners for Clearing — and they are also becoming increasingly competitive. Clearing's narrative must hold both truths: we are partner-respectful and we have a distinct, portable financial layer that no PMS can replicate.

The portability value proposition

Keeping accounting in Clearing — independent of the PMS — gives operators something no PMS-native accounting can: portability. When an operator wants to migrate their tech stack, their Clearing data stays whole. Their financial history, audit trail, owner records, and distributions are intact. That significantly reduces the burden of switching PMS — turning a major project into a reconnection.

This is a standalone Clearing value proposition that is distinct from Hostfully Accounting. It can be communicated to all prospects, including those evaluating or already using other PMS platforms. Operators who pay Clearing even when not actively using it — to hold their financial data — validate this value directly.

✓ Communicate this

Clearing integrates with leading PMS platforms. The operations layer and financial layer work together — and independently when needed.
Your accounting history travels with you. If you change your PMS, Clearing keeps your full audit trail intact.
Operators in Clearing can evaluate and switch PMS platforms with far less financial disruption. That's a feature, not an afterthought.
For standalone Clearing users: this is the financial operating system for your STR business, independent of any single PMS.

✕ Avoid this

Naming specific PMS platforms in negative comparisons in any external content.
Implying an operator made a bad choice by using PMS-native accounting — meet them where they are.
Over-rotating to anti-PMS language that could damage partner relationships, especially with Hostfully integration partners.
Forgetting to distinguish standalone Clearing from Hostfully Accounting — they are different products with different narratives.
Governance

Brand Checklist

Before any piece of content goes out the door, run it against this checklist. If you cannot answer yes to all of these, it needs revision.

Does this explain what Clearing does in plain, specific language — not generic fintech jargon?
Does it reflect both bookkeeping and reconciliation as distinct but related capabilities?
Does it carry the right signals of accounting rigor: audit-ready, role-based access, financial controls, reconciliation integrity?
Is urgency grounded in real operational pain — not manufactured fear or panic?
Does it treat PMS platforms as partners while clearly communicating Clearing's independent, portable financial layer?
Does the AI language describe outcomes (clean, reconciled, audit-ready books) not capabilities?
Is the voice precise, calm, and rigorous — without becoming heavy or corporate?
Does it use STR-specific financial language that operators and accountants recognize?
Is every specific claim sourced, qualified, or verifiable? No unattributed stats or superlatives.
Does it speak to the right audience for this piece — and reflect what that audience actually cares about?
Does the visual language use the approved color palette and typography? Zero em dashes in copy.
Does this look and sound like a modern fintech brand for serious STR operators — not generic SaaS?
When Clearing sounds precise and looks consistent, the brand earns the same trust the product promises.
— Clearing Brand Principle
